acceptance: A unit test with a stubbed API shows a wait of N cycles on an unchanged head makes the ruleset and trunk reads once, and the conditional reads return 304 without the code re-parsing a new body.
A test shows the cached ruleset or trunk read is discarded and re-read when the head changes, and that an arm is never decided on a body not confirmed current this cycle.
A before-and-after count of `gh` processes per wait cycle is recorded on this item using a stubbed or recorded run, and the reduction meets or beats 16% (the once-per-wait reads alone).
`make pr-arm` behaviour on the arming outcome lines is otherwise unchanged; existing `pr_arm` tests pass.
description:
Remedy (a) chosen by the owner on 2026-11-17 for shared-github-quota-and-transient-failure-owner-20261113. A 26-hour measurement (2026-11-15 to 2026-11-16) found about 30,000 core REST requests, one hourly window at the 5,000 limit, and `scripts/pr_arm.py` starting 65% of observed `gh` processes (5,886 of 9,040) from 14 concurrent worktrees. While waiting, `pr-arm` repeats every 180 seconds: paginated check-runs read (1,566 processes), `gh run list --workflow trunk.yml` (860), ruleset required-checks read (590), paginated ci-text-edit-refresh workflow-runs read (549), tracker index read (373), `gh pr view` (281).

Change. Inside one `arm_waiting` call: (1) read the ruleset required checks and the trunk workflow state once at the start and again only when the head changes or WAIT is half spent, not every cycle; (2) use conditional requests (If-None-Match with the stored ETag) for the check-runs, workflow-runs, index and pull-request reads, since a 304 does not count against the primary rate limit; (3) keep arming decisions based only on a successful, current read.

Expected saving, from the measurement, not yet confirmed: reading the ruleset and trunk once per wait removes about 1,450 of the 9,040 observed processes (16%); conditional requests on the other four reads address about 2,490 more (28%), together up to about 44% of observed `gh` calls. Paginated reads are several requests per process, so the true request saving may differ; the measurement tool does not see page counts.

Decision gates.
- Before editing, confirm with a stubbed or live call that a `gh api` conditional request returns 304 and that `gh` surfaces it so the code can reuse its cached body; if `gh` hides 304s, use `gh api -i` or a direct request, and say so here.
- Caching state across cycles must never make an arm decision on a read older than the current cycle for the same head: a cached body is reused only after a 304 for that exact request. If a request cannot be made conditional, it is read fresh.
- Any change to which checks must pass, or to the review-gate or trunk-gate rules, is out of scope; stop and report if the work seems to need one.
- Do together with pr-arm-github-rate-limit-backoff-20261112 only if both touch the same read helper; otherwise a separate pull request, serial, since `pr-arm` is a landing tool.

Guardrails.
- An unreadable or stale state is never a pass; arming still requires a successful current read of the trunk and review-gate state.
- No GitHub request is added to the wait loop; the number per cycle only goes down.
- No credentials, tokens or identities change under this item (option (b) was not chosen).
- No check is skipped or made non-blocking to save requests.
- Tests use a stubbed API; none calls GitHub.
